items.text: Fifteen ensembles of eight people, 120 in all, tapped on touchpads in booths round an octagonal table, out of direct sight of one another, each tap shown to all eight as a flash at one of eight lights. A trial of 68 seconds had 5 seconds of tapping at a comfortable rate with a person's own flashes alone, then 10 seconds paced by metronome flashes, the eight parted as two groups of four paced at 1.5 and 1.5, 1.65 and 1.35, or 1.8 and 1.2 hertz. Then came 50 seconds of seeing each other's taps, each person asked only to go on at the metronome's rate. Coordination formed regardless, in-phase the dominant pattern and a near antiphase pattern beside it, its epochs mostly transient or intermittent. At frequency differences of 0 and 0.3 hertz the two groups joined as one larger structure, and at 0.6 hertz they parted. Phase-locking within a group weakened with its frequency difference from the other group. Integration of the two groups parts from their segregation near a frequency difference of about 0.5 hertz.
